lines: No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.

Casey was visited by: Ellis, Blair.

Alex.feeling: Tense and murky: Drew's unverifiable Turkey claim looks suspicious, but Casey's death and the conflicting visit stories leave the final vote uncertain.

Blair.feeling: Tense but workable: I'm Meowfia with Ellis, Casey's wink went through, and Drew and Finley are now trading throws, which helps us.

Casey.feeling: Messy and tense: I'm dead, so I can't speak, and the table is split between a throw at Drew and a throw at Finley, with the Turkey and Eagle claims hard to check.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: the claims conflict, and two players are pushing a throw at me on thin evidence.

Ellis.feeling: Tense but going my way: Drew and Finley are throwing at each other and Blair is my partner, though I have to keep my Floofer role hidden.

Finley.feeling: Tense and muddled: Casey's death and the conflicting visit claims leave Drew as the only clear suspect, and the table has rallied behind a throw at Drew.

Alex.note: Final eggsecution: I'm throwing my three highest cards at Drew, the player I've been arguing against, since my stake banks at full value if Drew is Meowfia.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia; I'll throw at Drew, a Farm player, with a Wild card. If Drew is eggsecuted, Meowfia scores and my stake banks at double value, which is 0 here, so I lose nothing.

Casey.note: I'm dead, so my card throw counts only as a stake, not a vote. Drew's Turkey claim is the one we can't check and Finley's Eagle count fits, so I'll throw my only Wild at Drew for a low-risk stake.

Drew.note: Keeping the throw at Finley: my 8 returns if Finley is Farm, and only the 2 and the Wild are at risk.

Ellis.note: Throwing at Drew, the likely Farm target; staking two 7s so the highest returns if I miss.

Finley.note: I'm Farm and Drew's Turkey claim is the weakest read, so I'm throwing at Drew. Two high cards bank at full value if Drew is Meowfia, and a miss only costs me the two points they would have been in my nest.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Owl egg rules were hard to track: Blair and Ellis both gained eggs from visiting Casey, and it was unclear whether a Turkey's visitors or a Hawk's visit changed nests. The scoring of kept cards versus banked cards also took some reading.
Alex.fun: Round 2's Kookaburra reveal: I learned Drew was the Mouser, then the table turned on me and I was winked, which made the day feel like a real social fight.
Alex.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can check each other's claims without relying on guesses.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I openly outed Drew as the Mouser on day one of my turn, which probably made me a Wink target. I'd instead have waited and checked Drew's claim against others before drawing attention.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion was hard to act on: I got a dawn report saying Casey was the Turkey, and I couldn't tell whether that report was wrong.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when the table argued over whether Turkeys gain eggs from visits, and Ellis and Finley both admitted their egg counts were misread.
Blair.change: Make the Kookaburra's confusion visible to its owner, or tell them which part of the report is wrong, so players can plan around it.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Casey, a real Farm Owl, and falsely claimed Kookaburra. I should have saved the Wink for a riskier Farm claim, like Drew's Turkey, and stayed quiet about my role.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey and Kookaburra reports were hard to sort out, since a Turkey gains nothing and visitors gain eggs, which made a flat nest look like nobody visited. The Sphinx and Floofer also gave little to check.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when two visitors to Alex both got hugged, so I reasoned that Alex was the Floofer and the table voted Alex out. That was a clean deduction, and it was right.
Casey.change: Show each player's role-visit history at dawn, or give a clearer public record of who visited whom, so claims can be checked more easily.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw only one card at Finley, who was Meowfia; I should have thrown three to bank more points when I was right.

Drew.confusing: The Kookaburra's "confused" reports made it hard to tell which claims were reliable, especially Blair's Owl claim versus Casey's. Casey's Turkey and Owl claims also swapped back and forth in Round 2.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well: the hug read on Alex was right, and the table converged on Alex from several independent visits. Winking Alex in Round 2 to stop a lynch on me was also satisfying.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so claims can be checked without relying on egg counts and guesses.
Drew.regret: In Round 3 I backed a throw at Finley and staked my 8 on a Turkey claim nobody could verify, when I should have pushed the throw at Ellis, who was the Meowfia Floofer, and argued from the hug pattern.

Ellis.confusing: The Grudge bonus and how the final score was built (bonus points on top of the pile and kept cards) weren't explained, and I only learned Turkeys pay visitors after I'd already misread my own egg gain.
Ellis.fun: Round 1: two visitors to Alex both got hugged, so I pushed the Floofer read, the table followed, and Farm won.
Ellis.change: Show each player's score breakdown and the Grudge rule in the rules up front, so the endgame isn't a surprise.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I publicly claimed my egg came from a correct Tit guess, which was wrong and cost me credibility; I'd check the role's payout rules before making a claim.

Finley.confusing: The Sphinx's night choice was hard to use well: I named a farm role without knowing who held it, and the dawn report only told me the role's holder after the fact. The egg rules for the Turkey and Hawk were also confusing until the table worked them out on the day.
Finley.fun: The Round 3 day, where Farm players traded Eagle and Hawk claims and Drew's unverifiable Turkey story became the target. Watching the throw counts reveal alignment without any values was tense.
Finley.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so that claims like the Turkey and Owl could be checked without guessing from egg counts.
Finley.regret: In Round 2 I spent my stake on a throw at Blair, a Farm player, and then had no way to undo it when Finley was eggsecuted. I would have thrown zero cards and stayed quiet, keeping my nest intact.
